title: Poulaphouca
html_source: Poulaphouca is a word used several times in Circe (Ch. 15). It refers to a scenic area on the border betwee County Wicklow and County Kildare near the head of the Liffey that was lost with the construction of the Poulaphouca Reservoir (depicted in the northwest of the county in the map below; created by the dam depicted below). Name from the Irish: Poll an Phúca, meaning “the Púca’s hole” (Puca being a kind of nature spirit in Celtic mythology).
